commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Keep tied results in stored order
commitResults.messageBody:
The comparator from a name search only compares match cost, so persons
who match equally well have no defined order. Replacing one, as `fav`
does, can move it among its ties, and a search after `list sorted`
keeps the alphabetical order for ties. An index can then hit the wrong
contact, and the UG promises that ties keep their usual order.

Let's break ties by position in the filtered list in ModelManager, so
that every comparator given to the model gets a fully defined order.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Correct the fuzzy search steps
commitResults.messageBody:
Step 1 leaves out that `/room` searches also have no comparator. Step 5
says `yeo` is 1 typo from `yeoh`, but it matches first as the start of
the word.

Let's add `/room` and describe how `yeo` really matches.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Simplify the fuzzy search diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The diagram is 1687px wide but shown at 740px, so its text is hard to
read. Most of its width goes to parser creation and CommandResult, which
the general logic diagram already covers.

Let's keep only the predicate, the comparator and the matching loop.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Tidy the find section
commitResults.messageBody:
The section runs to about 790 words with no screenshot. Its four kinds
of search sit under bold labels that readers cannot jump to, and some
rules are repeated.

Let's make each kind of search a real subheading, keep each rule in one
place, and add a screenshot of a name search.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Reject unknown prefixes
commitResults.messageBody:
A mistyped prefix, as in `find /name Amy /rom B-204`, is treated as
search text. The search then reports `No contacts found` and empties the
list, which looks like a valid search with no matches.

No word of a valid name, tag, phone or room starts with `/`, so such a
word is always a mistake. Let's reject it with the usage message and
leave the list unchanged, as other commands do.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Warn about field names in edit notes
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG warns about field names in notes only under `add`, where no
saved data is overwritten. In `edit`, a field name in a note silently
renames the contact or removes a field, while reporting success. `/tag`
after `/note` also gets the note's message rather than the documented
invalid format message.

The parser cannot tell a field from note text, so let's warn about both
under `edit`.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Explain how note length is counted
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG allows 200 characters of any kind, but a note of 101 emoji is
rejected as too long, because most emoji take 2 or more Java characters.

Counting what users see as one character needs more than a small change
to the shared length check, so let's state the rule in the UG.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Use distinct names in the note tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The note tests add Wei Ling more than once, so the later cases that
should succeed report `Contact already exists.` instead.

Let's give each successful add its own name.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Correct the note text
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual test for `edit 1 /note see /docs` expects the `edit` usage,
but the app shows the note's own message, which is the intended one. The
Tag feature section also leaves `/note` out of the keywords `add` takes.

Let's correct both and add manual tests for field names in edit notes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag, Room: Require a letter or digit
commitResults.messageBody:
A tag or room made only of hyphens, or a tag that is only an accent
mark, is accepted, and such a tag shows as a nearly empty badge. Rooms
also reject `#`, although `#03-12` is a common unit format in Singapore.

Let's require at least one letter or digit in both fields and allow `#`
in rooms. Saved data with such a tag or room becomes invalid, so the UG
now says so.

commitResults.messageTitle: Validation: Clarify tag and character errors
commitResults.messageBody:
`add` reports a tag given twice as `Contact already has this tag.`,
although the contact does not exist yet. Invalid tags, rooms and phones
only say they contain invalid characters, so users cannot tell what to
change.

Let's use `toggle`'s repeated-tag wording in `add` too, with the message
now in Tag so both share it, and list the allowed characters in each
message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag: Treat equivalent Unicode forms as equal
commitResults.messageBody:
`é` can be typed as one character or as `e` and a combining mark. These
two forms look the same, but count as different tags, so a contact can
show `Café` twice, and `find /tag` matches only the form typed.

Let's normalize names to NFC in Tag#toComparisonKey, which every tag
comparison goes through, so a tag still displays as typed.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Correct the tag validation diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The diagram checks for a repeated tag before creating the Tag, although
the code creates it first, and it leaves out the title-case length check.
Its separate error paths make it wide, and its colors differ from the
other activity diagrams.

Let's show the real order, group the invalid value checks, which the DG
text already lists, and drop `skin rose`.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Correct the tag manual tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The tag filter tests search for `friends`, which no sample contact has,
and expect the usage message for a repeated `/tag`, although the app
names the repeated prefix, as the UG says.

Let's use a tag the sample data has and give the repeated prefix its own
expected error.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Fix the command summary
commitResults.messageBody:
The summary has two Find rows, and the second leaves out `/room`. It also
has an `Edit (suspended)` row, although `edit` works, which contradicts
the normal Edit row.

Let's remove the outdated Find row and the suspended Edit row.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Use the product name throughout
commitResults.messageBody:
Parts of the UG still call the product AddressBook or Address Book, the
name of the app it was based on, while the rest says RAcontact.

Let's use RAcontact in the text. File names such as addressbook.json
stay, as they are not the product name.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name: Accept real names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names only accept ASCII letters, digits and spaces, so an RA cannot save
names such as `Kumar s/o Rajan`, `O'Brien`, `Mary-Jane Lee`, `José
García` or `李小明`, although tags accept letters in any language.

Let's accept letters, marks and digits in any language, and `'`, `-`,
`.` and `/`, with each word starting with a letter or digit. No word can
then start with `/`, so a name is never mistaken for a field. `add`,
`edit`, `emergency` and data files share the rule. The UG now lists it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name: Normalize names and check their length
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file can hold a name over the 100-character limit, or `Sarah
Tan` and `Sarah  Tan` as two contacts, which `add` treats as duplicates.
`add` only applies these rules while parsing.

Let's collapse whitespace and check the length in Name, as Tag and Room
do, so typed and loaded names follow the same rules and the existing
duplicate check catches both spellings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Person card: Wrap long names
commitResults.messageBody:
A long name within the 100-character limit is cut off with `...` on a
narrow window, while notes and emergency details wrap, so an RA cannot
read the whole name.

Let's wrap the name label too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find: Normalize Unicode whitespace before parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
Find checks its arguments for prefixes using ASCII whitespace only.

After a non-breaking space, a mistyped or second prefix such as /rom
or /room is treated as search text, so the user gets a wrong search
instead of the usage error.

Let's collapse whitespace before tokenizing, as add and the
index-based commands already do, so all commands read prefixes alike.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Replace "address book" with "contact list"
commitResults.messageBody:
Five sentences in the User Guide still use AB3's term "address book".

The rest of the guide talks about RAcontact's contact list, so the old
term may confuse readers about what these commands act on.

Let's use "contact list" throughout. The addressbook.jar and
addressbook.json file names stay, as they are the real file names.

commitResults.messageTitle: UI: Fix window title and help window keyboard use
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window title is "Address App", left over from AB3. The help
window cannot be closed with the keyboard, as Esc does nothing and
focus lands on its Copy URL button. Running help while the window is
minimized leaves it minimized, even though the result says it opened.

RAs on duty type fast and should not need the mouse to get back to the
command box, or to wonder where the help window went.

Let's title the window RAcontact, let Esc close the help window, and
restore the help window when help is run while it is minimized. The
known issue about the minimized help window is removed from the UG.

Fixes #159

commitResults.messageTitle: Edit: Report unchanged contacts and very large indexes
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit reports "Edited person" even when nothing changed, such as
removing a room the contact does not have. An index too large for an
int, such as 2147483648, gives "Invalid command format" while
2147483647 gives "The person index provided is invalid."

The success message misleads an RA into thinking a contact was
updated, and the index error depends on a limit the UG never mentions.

Let's report "NAME already has these details. No changes made." when
an edit changes nothing, and parse a positive integer too large for an
int as the largest index, which is past the end of any list. This
covers every command that uses ParserUtil#parseIndex, so tests that
expected the old format error now expect the invalid index error.

Fixes #166

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag: Match dotless i tags by their typed spelling
commitResults.messageBody:
A tag typed as the Turkish dotless "ı" is stored title-cased as "I".
The comparison key only lowercases, so the stored tag becomes "i"
while the typed "ı" stays "ı", and find /tag ı finds nothing.

A tag that was accepted should be found by the same text used to add
it, as the UG promises case-insensitive matching for any language.

Let's uppercase before lowercasing when building the comparison key,
so a letter and its title-cased form always give the same key. Every
tag comparison goes through this key, so find, toggle and archive
selection are all fixed.

Fixes #188

commitResults.messageTitle: Logic: Keep help available when saving fails
commitResults.messageBody:
Every command saves the address book before its result reaches the
UI. When saving fails, help throws the save error and its window
never opens, even though help changes no data.

Help is what an RA reaches for when something goes wrong, so it should
still work then.

Let's return the help result before saving. Exit still saves first,
so a failing save keeps the app open instead of losing edits whose
saves already failed without the RA noticing. The UG documents both.

Fixes #150

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Replace template placeholders with real instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual test for missing and corrupted data files is still the AB3
template text, and several sections end with placeholders such as
"{ more test cases ... }".

A tester following the DG cannot run the data file test or judge its
result, and the leftover placeholders make the guide look unfinished.

Let's describe how to simulate a missing, corrupted and invalid data
file in a disposable folder, with the expected result of each,
including when the file is created or overwritten. The remaining
template placeholders are removed.

Fixes #189

commitResults.messageTitle: Tag: Match capital sharp s tags by their typed spelling
commitResults.messageBody:
The comparison key uppercases then lowercases a name. A tag typed as
"ẞ" is stored as "ß", which becomes "ss", but the typed "ẞ" stays
uppercase and becomes "ß", so find /tag ẞ misses the tag it created.

Every accepted tag should be found by the text used to add it.

Let's lowercase first, then uppercase and lowercase again, so a typed
name and its title-cased stored form always share a key. A test now
checks this for every valid single-character tag.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Describe very large indexes as invalid indexes
commitResults.messageBody:
Very large indexes such as fav 2147483648 now report an invalid index,
but the UG and DG still say they give an invalid command format.

Let's update the fav section of the UG, the delete-by-name
implementation note and the favourites manual tests to match.
